title: Research notes: Hartford and Fort Hartford
summary: Sources for Hartford’s founding as Fort Hartford on the Rough River and its rise as the Ohio County seat. Swapped in for Taylorsville, which already has a story (2026-09-10).

items.text: Part of Gabriel Madison’s 4,000-acre Virginia grant; surveyed 1782; evidence of a 1782 settlement, first fortified place in the lower Green River Valley.
William Smeathers’ account of building “a fort at Hartford on Rough Creek” in 1782–83; stockade believed to stand on the bluff now used by the water plant.
Barnett’s Station raid, April 1790: two children killed, Hannah Barnett (10) held captive six months.
Ohio County formed December 1798 from Hardin County, named for the Ohio River; first county court 1799.
Madison’s land grant for the town; seat chosen the year after the county’s formation.
Log courthouse and jail 1799–1800; collapsed 1813; salvaged timber burned to celebrate Perry’s Lake Erie victory.
Post office Hartford Court House 1801; town incorporated 1808.
Marker: name from the river ford where animals crossed; Wikipedia: origin uncertain, ford or a ferry-keeping settler.
First covered bridge over the Rough River here, 1823; earlier crossings by ford or ferry.
Which nation’s warriors raided Hartford and Barnett’s Station: not stated in the sources, so not named.

timeline.event: Madison grant surveyed; first settlement and fort.
First county court; Madison gives land for the town.

people.name: Gabriel Madison
people.role: Virginia grantee, gave land for the town

openQuestions: A primary record for the exact date the first fort was built.
The true origin of the name Hartford.
